steps.note: In Mimolette, mites feed on the rind during ageing and pit it, which lets air in.

steps.name: turn and brush
steps.note: The cheeses are turned and brushed regularly to keep the mites in check.

processing.text: Casu marzu is the other way: a pecorino with a hole in its rind is left to the cheese fly (Piophila casei), whose larvae break the paste down until it is creamy.

links.name: The Cheese Scientist: Mimolette, a story of cheese mites

sources.text: Mimolette is a cow's-milk cheese ripened 3 to 18 months or more with mites, regularly turned and brushed; casu marzu is a pecorino opened to cheese flies. A blog source, so low authority. Neither is made from a hard cheese in the sense used here; the arrow's start from "hard" is loose.
